## TL;DR

Task #1092 adds `repoos release email --preview <version>` so maintainers can inspect a rendered release email from the terminal without sending mail. The command calls the existing `GET /api/release/email/preview` route through the same `RepoOsApi` client other control-plane CLIs use, prints subject then HTML then plain text (or `--json` for the full body), and registers the route in `src/cli/api-route-parity.ts`. Tests in `release-email.test.ts` cover a happy path and a missing-version error. Scoped `repoos check` passed locally after formatting; remote validation followed the normal queue.

## Work and rationale

Release emails landed in #1071 with a preview API and a Releases-page Preview button, but the only CLI path was `repoos api GET /api/release/email/preview?version=…`, which is easy to forget and tripped the parity rule’s expectation of a first-class command. The task scope was intentionally narrow: no send path, no new renderer, no runtime dependencies.

I added `src/commands/release.ts` with `cmdRelease`, wired it from `src/cli/index.ts`, and documented it under Setup in `src/cli/help.ts` next to `upgrade`. The parser accepts only `release email --preview <version>` today so future `repoos release …` subcommands can grow without changing the top-level dispatch. `--port` and `--json` match the other server-backed commands.

The HTTP route was the right boundary. `previewReleaseEmail` already lives in `release-email.ts` and is shared with the UI, but the acceptance criteria asked explicitly for the preview route. Using `RepoOsApi.requestOk` keeps auth, dev backdoor refresh, and error shaping identical to `repoos handoff-status` and `repoos landable`. When the server is down, the command fails with the same “start `repoos serve`” guidance rather than silently reimplementing config reads in the CLI.

Human-readable output prints `Subject:` on its own line, then a blank line, then the HTML, another blank line, then the text body—enough structure for piping HTML to a file or eyeballing the plain-text part in a log. `--json` dumps the API payload for scripting.

Parity is recorded as `exact("GET", "/api/release/email/preview")` under `FILE_CLI_MATCHERS`. The blanket `under("/api/release")` UI exemption from #1071 still covers the rest of the release surface (cut, send, etc.); only preview needed a dedicated CLI entry called out in the task.

`docs/releases.md` no longer lists the missing CLI among known gaps; it points maintainers at the new command instead.

## Approaches tried

The main fork was **in-process render versus HTTP**. Calling `previewReleaseEmail(loadConfig(), version)` directly would work offline and would match some file-level commands (`repoos list` never hits `/api/tasks`). I rejected that because the spec named the preview route and the team already treats “CLI parity” as “there is a command that exercises the same server behavior the UI uses,” not a duplicate code path that could drift if the handler gains guards later.

Nested dispatch could have been folded into `control-api.ts` with other `RepoOsApi` commands. A separate `release.ts` keeps the namespace clear for future release tooling without growing an already large module.

## Challenges and blockers

The first scoped `repoos check` failed only on `check-fmt:check`; `bun run fmt` reformatted the new command file (a wrapped `if` in the port parser). No logic change.

Remote validation queued normally; one runner hung during the first full check and the orchestrator retried on another host, which is expected infrastructure behavior rather than a code defect.

The command requires a running control plane, same as previewing through the UI’s authenticated fetches. That is consistent with other release operations that read live `release-history.json` through server config context.

## Key learnings

Small parity gaps are worth closing with thin CLI wrappers: the implementation is mostly argument parsing and stdout formatting, but it removes a recurring review finding from #1071 and gives operators a stable interface documented in `repoos help`.

Placing tests beside the release-email suite keeps mocked `RepoOsApi` examples next to the route tests that define preview semantics; the CLI tests assert the exact query string and exit codes without standing up a server.

When adding a targeted command for one route, prefer an explicit `exact()` parity entry over relying on a broad `under()` prefix so the next engineer can see which CLI owns which endpoint.
